I'm an OB-GYN. I've had a hysterectomy. And when the things I'd spent twelve years telling women to buy stopped working on me, I sat down and read every label on that shelf.

Here they are, ranked worst to best.

My name is Dr. Chantelle Anderson. Board-certified OB-GYN, 12 years in practice. 

I had my hysterectomy at 45, and within a year I was standing in the same drugstore aisle I'd been sending my own patients to since residency, buying the same products I'd been recommending, with the same result they'd been reporting back to me for over a decade.

Nothing.

So I did the thing I should have done years earlier. I bought the five best-sellers. I read every ingredient list.

And I compared them against what the published literature actually says the problem is.

Three things I want to give you today:

Why almost everything in that aisle fails
The three things nearly every product leaves out
The five that came out on top, in order

Now, here's why almost everything on that shelf fails.

I spent years buying every arthritis supplement I could find because I was desperate to avoid taking ibuprofen every day.

Then I came across a rheumatologist explaining why.

He rated all the supplements I'd been taking, and honestly it finally made sense.

Collagen wasn't addressing inflammation.

Glucosamine had mixed evidence.

Fish oil wasn't dosed high enough in most products.

Even turmeric wasn't enough because most brands only contain 2-6% curcumin, and curcumin only tackles one part of the inflammation.

The ingredient I'd never even heard of was Boswellia.

It works completely differently to curcumin, which is why taking both together made so much more sense than taking turmeric on its own.

That's why I switched to Nova's Curcumin + Boswellia.

It combines 95% standardized curcumin, full-strength Boswellia and black pepper extract to help absorption.

Within a few weeks I wasn't reaching for ibuprofen every day anymore. My mornings became easier, I was moving better, and my joints finally felt like they were improving instead of getting worse.

If you've tried all the usual arthritis supplements without much success, this combination is honestly worth looking into.

Iron isn’t a diva. It’s just following hepcidin’s schedule. 💅

You’ve probably heard of ferritin – it’s the protein that binds to iron and stores it in your body. A ferritin test is one way to measure how much iron you have stored. 

But Hepcidin is the hormone your liver makes to regulate HOW much iron gets in. It follows a daily rhythm, lowest in the morning and peaking in the afternoon. If you take iron every day, hepcidin doesn’t get much time to reset. 

That’s the idea behind Iron BioSeries™, the world’s first 48-hour dosing routine with BioSeries™ technology, designed for optimal absorption and minimal GI discomfort.*

Ever go to bed absolutely wrecked…
but your brain decides it’s the perfect time to start thinking about everything?

Work.
Bills.
That awkward thing you said five years ago.

Next thing you know, it’s 3am.

Here’s something most people don’t realise:

It’s not always stress causing this.

Very often, the body is simply low on magnesium — the mineral responsible for calming the nervous system and helping your body wind down for sleep.

So naturally, many people try magnesium supplements.

But here’s where things go wrong.

Most magnesium tablets absorb very poorly.

A large portion of the mineral passes straight through the digestive system before your body can actually use it.

Which is why many people take magnesium for weeks… and still find themselves staring at the ceiling at night.

Now more people across Ireland are discovering a different approach.

Instead of pills, they’re switching to liquid magnesium drops.

Oriel Sleep Drops contain deep-sea magnesium with trace minerals, designed to absorb far more efficiently than traditional supplements.

Just add a few drops to water about 30 minutes before bed.

No pills.
No bloating.
No complicated routine.

Just a simple way to help your body relax — the way it’s supposed to.

Sometimes better sleep isn’t about trying harder.

It’s about giving your body the mineral it’s been missing.

“My fish oil keeps repeating on me.” “I get fish oil burps hours after I take it” “I’ve given up on omega-3s, they all taste awful.” 🤢

I hear these in clinic all the time, and the reason behind them is simple 💡

In basic terms ➡️ in the same way properly fresh fish doesn’t taste fishy, fresh fish oil won’t either.

Omega-3 fats are delicate. Once they’re exposed to air, light or heat, they start to go off, in the same way any oil can turn rancid. 
As they break down, they create compounds which have a strong fishy taste and smell.
So a fishy fish oil is a sign it isn’t as fresh as it should be ❌

For some people digestion plays a part too. 
Lower stomach acid levels, which can happen when you’re busy, stressed, or have just exercised hard, means the oil sits in your stomach for longer. And then it’s more likely to come back up. 
Taking it during a meal that contains some fat will help it move through with your food to prevent that ✅

I spent 22 years treating arthritis. Then at 54, I got it myself.

I did everything I'd told my patients to do — perfectly. And my joints kept getting worse anyway.

That's when I realised I'd been giving people the wrong advice for two decades 👇

Let me explain what almost no one gets told at diagnosis.
Arthritis pain isn't caused by one thing. It's caused by two completely different types of inflammation — and they behave nothing alike.

The FIRST type is the one you feel. The swelling. The heat. The ache that flares when you overdo it and settles when you rest. This is the one everything targets — the painkillers, the gels, the turmeric. It's the loud one.

The SECOND type is the one you can't feel. And it's the dangerous one.

It doesn't cause swelling. It doesn't cause pain. Instead, it quietly releases enzymes that break down your cartilage — the smooth cushion that stops your bones grinding against each other. And here's the part I need you to understand, because it's why people come to me too late:

Cartilage has no nerve endings.

So while this second inflammation is doing the real, permanent damage… you feel absolutely nothing. No warning. No ache telling you to stop. Nothing — right up until the cushion is worn so thin that bone starts touching bone.

THAT is the day the pain "suddenly" arrives. On the stairs. Getting out of the car. And everyone says the same thing: "it came out of nowhere."

It didn't. It had been building silently for years.

Off the coast of South Africa there is an orca called Starboard. Marine biologists have watched him kill great white sharks, take the liver out in under two minutes, and swim away leaving hundreds of pounds of shark floating untouched. He is not being wasteful. He is being precise. The liver is the part worth having.

Wolves open the belly first and the dominant pair eats the liver, heart and kidneys while the muscle meat goes to the bottom of the pack. Lions do the same. Hunter-gatherer cultures ate the heart and liver in the field before they carried the animal home, and the organs went to the hunters, the elders, the pregnant women and the children. Then in about one generation we reversed it. After the war, steak became the thing you ate once you had made it. Organs became the embarrassing food your grandmother cooked. We threw away the part every predator fights for and started calling the leftovers the good stuff.

When estrogen drops, all three go at the same time. Shorter growth phase, thinner foundation, less protection from the hormone that miniaturizes follicles.

One decline, three failures. That's why it shows up so fast, and why the topical stuff never got to it.

A nourishing and balanced meal, perfect for dinner, and ideal for calming and relaxing the body after a long day. It contains high quality protein, it is rich in Omega-3s, Magnesium, B vitamins, and slow releasing carbohydrates - all of which help support healthy cortisol levels and ease the nervous system before bed.

Ingredients (serves 2):

2 wild caught trout fillets (or salmon)
Salt & black pepper, to taste
2 sweet potatoes
Dash of plant-based milk (I used almond milk)
3-4 generous handfuls of fresh spinach
2 tbsp butter
2 tbsp lemon juice
Small handful fresh parsley, finely chopped

Instructions:
Prepare the sweet potato mash: peel the sweet potatoes, cut them into 2-3cm chunks. Bring a pot of water to a boil, add a generous pinch of salt, and then add the sweet potatoes. Cook for 12-15min, or until the potatoes are soft when pierced with a fork. Drain and return to the pot or a medium sized bowl. Add a dash of plant based milk and a pinch of salt. Mash until smooth.

Cook the trout: season both trout fillet sides with salt and black pepper. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with some olive oil or butter. Place the trout skin-side down and cook for 3-4 minutes until the skin is crisp. Flip and cook for another 2-3 minutes, or until the flesh flakes gently. Remove the cooked trout from the pan, and add 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp of lemon juice, and chopped parsley to the pan for a few seconds.

Wilt the spinach: lightly saute the spinach for 1-2 minutes. Season with salt

One supplement for gut health, hormones, thyroid support, energy, stress, hair, skin AND sleep? That’s a red flag.

When a single powder or pill promises to address almost every area of your health, it’s worth questioning how much it can realistically do for any one of them.

A long ingredient list can look impressive, but more ingredients doesn’t necessarily mean a better formula. There’s only so much you can fit into a scoop or capsule, and trying to include dozens of ingredients can mean there simply isn’t enough room for meaningful amounts of each.

You shouldn’t need to become a nutritionist or spend hours deciphering dosages to choose a good supplement. Instead, look at the bigger picture: Does this product have a clear purpose? Do the ingredients make sense for that purpose? Are the claims realistic?

There is no magic powder that can do everything.

If something sounds too good to be true, it usually is. Like anything in life, when you try to be everything to everyone, you often end up not doing anything particularly well.

I spent 22 years treating arthritis. Then at 54, I got it myself.

I did everything I'd told my patients to do — perfectly. And my joints kept getting worse anyway.

That's when I realised I'd been giving people the wrong advice for two decades 👇

Let me explain what almost no one gets told at diagnosis.
Arthritis pain isn't caused by one thing. It's caused by two completely different types of inflammation — and they behave nothing alike.

The FIRST type is the one you feel. The swelling. The heat. The ache that flares when you overdo it and settles when you rest. This is the one everything targets — the painkillers, the gels, the turmeric. It's the loud one.

The SECOND type is the one you can't feel. And it's the dangerous one.

It doesn't cause swelling. It doesn't cause pain. Instead, it quietly releases enzymes that break down your cartilage — the smooth cushion that stops your bones grinding against each other. And here's the part I need you to understand, because it's why people come to me too late:

Cartilage has no nerve endings.

So while this second inflammation is doing the real, permanent damage… you feel absolutely nothing. No warning. No ache telling you to stop. Nothing — right up until the cushion is worn so thin that bone starts touching bone.

THAT is the day the pain "suddenly" arrives. On the stairs. Getting out of the car. And everyone says the same thing: "it came out of nowhere."

It didn't. It had been building silently for years.

Why Acid Blockers Don't Fix GERD

The most misunderstood reason why acid reflux does not stop? Mucin hyposecretion.

Think of it as the erosion of your gut's defense system...

The clearest sign is that non-stop burning in your stomach and chest that outlasts every antacid in your medicine cabinet.

See, your body naturally produces mucin. It sits between your tissue and stomach acid.

When production is healthy, acid stays harmless.

Food passes through. Nothing burns.

But years of reflux, stress, and certain medications can slowly disrupt that production.

When that happens, coating thins. And eventually, acid that's always there starts burning tissue that used to be completely protected.

Which is why acid blockers like PPIs only help temporarily.

Sure, they lower the acid…

But they never restore the mucin your body stopped producing enough of.

So the burning fades for a while. Then comes right back.

Every time.

The Real Reason Your Hair Is Thinning After 40

Menopausal hair thinning is real, it's common, and most products aimed at it don't address the cause.

The cause is hormonal. Declining estrogen shortens your hair's growth phase, so you shed faster than you regrow.

PERI/MENO Essentials was formulated to support your hair through that exact transition, from within.

If your hair changed and nothing's helped, it's because you've been treating the wrong layer.

I knew perimenopause was doing it. I wanted to know how, because I was tired of scalp treatments I had to reapply every single day.

Here's what I found: hair follicles are estrogen-sensitive tissue. Estrogen does three separate jobs up there at once — it extends the growth phase, it keeps the collagen layer of the scalp thick (that's the follicle's actual home), and it buffers follicles against DHT.

When estrogen drops, all three go at the same time. Shorter growth phase, thinner foundation, less protection from the hormone that miniaturizes follicles.

One decline, three failures. That's why it shows up so fast, and why the topical stuff never got to it.
